jobs.title: Managing Director, Discovery and Insight
jobs.description:
About Ted

TED is on a mission to discover and spread ideas that spark imagination, embrace possibility, and catalyze impact. Our organization is devoted to curiosity, reason, wonder, and the pursuit of knowledge — without an agenda. We welcome people from every discipline and culture who seek a deeper understanding of the world and connection with others, and we invite everyone to engage with ideas and activate them in your community.

About The Audacious Project

The Audacious Project is a collaborative funding platform that invites visionary changemakers to imagine their boldest ideas to solve the world’s most urgent challenges.

Housed at TED, the nonprofit dedicated to the belief that ideas change everything, Audacious works to surface ideas that are breathtakingly ambitious yet achievable and brings together a community of philanthropists to unlock the funding needed to make them real. Each year, Audacious selects a cohort of extraordinary leaders from around the world — visionaries with proximity to the problems they're solving, and bold plans to shift systems, lift up communities, and contribute to a healthier planet.

Since its launch in 2018, Audacious has helped to catalyze more than $8B for over 70 projects across a range of issue areas. Rooted in TED's belief that ideas can come from anywhere, Audacious focuses on the strength of the idea and the team behind it, not a fixed issue area. Funded projects span science, climate, technology, health, social safety net and justice.

jobs.title: Temporary In-Person Event Executive Assistant  to the CEO - Stanford, California
jobs.description:
About 2Gether-International

2Gether-International (2GI) is the leading accelerator for disabled entrepreneurs, dedicated to fostering economic empowerment and innovation. Our flagship 10-week Accelerator Program equips disabled founders with the skills, mentorship, and resources they need to build and scale high-impact ventures. Running three accelerator cohorts annually, we maintain a thriving community that provides ongoing support, networking opportunities, and access to funding.

Through strategic partnerships with industry leaders, we aim to drive meaningful change and create inclusive economic opportunities.

We are seeking a reliable, adaptable, and professional Temporary In-Person Event Executive Assistant to the CEO to assist our CEO, Diego Mariscal, during conferences, events, and work-related travel.

About the Role

This is a unique opportunity to support a globally recognized disability entrepreneur and nonprofit leader while gaining access to high-level conference, networking opportunities, and professional events that many people would not otherwise have the opportunity to attend.

As an In-Person Event Executive Assistant to the CEO, you will support Diego Mariscal from September 18–21, 2026, during the 7th Annual Stanford Neurodiversity Summit. Throughout the summit, you will assist Diego with travel logistics, meetings, networking events, speaking engagements, and other event-related activities. Diego uses an electronic wheelchair, so this role requires someone who is comfortable assisting with accessibility logistics, coordinating transportation, navigating conference venues, and adapting quickly as schedules and priorities change throughout the day.

You will meet Diego at the airport upon his arrival and provide support throughout the duration of the summit and travel schedule, including accompanying him back to the airport upon his departure.

This role requires someone who is dependable, flexible, professional, calm under pressure, and comfortable making last-minute adjustments. It is not a traditional caregiving role. Instead, it is best suited for someone who is proactive, highly organized, resourceful, and excited to be part of a fast-paced, mission-driven environment while supporting a globally recognized disability entrepreneur and nonprofit leader.

Responsibilities

Meet Diego at the airport upon arrival and accompany him back to the airport upon departure
Assist with luggage, lifting luggage, transportation of Diego’s electronic wheelchair, and hotel arrival/departure logistics, including helping unpack and organize belongings as needed
Coordinate wheelchair-accessible transportation including local metro, taxis, rideshares, and other travel logistics
Assist Diego during conferences, meetings, networking events, and travel
Help navigate conference venues, hotels, airports, restaurants, and event spaces
Assist with accessibility-related logistics and problem-solving throughout the day
Help ensure smooth transitions between meetings, speaking engagements, and event sessions
Run errands and assist with logistical tasks throughout the day as needed
Provide on-the-ground support during conferences and travel
Be responsive and adaptable as schedules and priorities shift throughout the day
Occasionally assist with light administrative or coordination support during events
Maintain professionalism and discretion while interacting with partners, sponsors, donors, executives, and other high-level stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting individuals with physical disabilities is a plus
Experience working with clients or individuals with Cerebral Palsy is helpful but not required
Experience in hospitality, customer service, accessibility support, executive support, event coordination, or caregiving is a plus
Strong communication and interpersonal skills
Comfortable navigating busy conferences and event spaces
Strong problem-solving abilities
Able to think quickly and proactively
Comfortable with schedule changes and last-minute adjustments
Comfortable working extended hours during conferences, travel days, and event schedules when needed
Speaking both English and Spanish is preferred, but Spanish is not required

Ideal Candidate

Reliable, professional, and highly adaptable
Calm under pressure and comfortable in fast-paced environments
Organized and resourceful
Friendly and personable while maintaining professionalism
Passionate about disability inclusion and mission-driven work
Interested in networking, conferences, entrepreneurship, and nonprofit leadership

Compensation & Perks

Flat compensation of $600 USD for the event.
Depending on the CEO’s travel schedule and event needs, workdays may extend beyond traditional business hours
Conference or event registration will be fully covered
Opportunity to attend high-level conferences, networking events, receptions, and speaking engagements
Opportunity to network with nonprofit leaders, corporate executives, entrepreneurs, investors, philanthropists, and social impact leaders
Exposure to leaders in disability innovation, entrepreneurship, social impact, technology, venture capital, and nonprofit leadership

Unique opportunity to gain access to rooms, conversations, and experiences that many people would not otherwise have access to The 7th Annual Stanford Neurodiversity Summit brings together leaders, researchers, disability advocates, educators, innovators, entrepreneurs, nonprofit organizations, and changemakers focused on neurodiversity, accessibility, inclusion, and innovation.

Additional Details

This is a temporary contract role supporting the CEO exclusively during the Stanford Neurodiversity Summit in Stanford, California from September 18–21, 2026.
Event support will take place over four consecutive days.
Some days may require early mornings, evenings, or extended hours depending on event logistics
Prior experience is helpful but not required for the right candidate

Onboarding Process

Once selected, the Director of Operations will schedule an introductory meeting between the In-Person Event Executive Assistant to the CEO and Diego prior to the event. This meeting will provide an opportunity to:
Get to know one another
Review event logistics and schedules
Discuss expectations and communication preferences
Review accessibility and transportation needs
Answer questions prior to the event or travel dates

To Apply

Please email all application materials to:
kara@2gether-international.org

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
Job Summary

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), an affiliate of General Atomics, is a world leader in proven, reliable remotely piloted aircraft and tactical reconnaissance radars, as well as advanced high-resolution surveillance systems.

This position typically reports to a senior manager or senior program manager and is responsible for planning, managing, and overseeing the technical performance of one or more significant program(s) or one or more developing engineering program(s), usually contained at one primary location. The Program Director oversees all phases of the program(s) from initiation through delivery. The role directs programs which represent significant future growth in several distinct developing products or components and applies new technologies or methods to coordinate applications across program requirements. Objectives are typically accomplished through subordinate managers. The program(s) under this role are likely to be a factor in the company’s strategic business objectives. The position may be responsible for decisions where erroneous decisions could cause substantial expenditure of time and resources.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Direct all phases of the program(s) from conceptualization through completion, including acquisition, planning, and managing technical performance to ensure quality, business, and financial objectives are attained.
Develop and coordinate new program plans or delivery methods with little precedence for coordination across distinctive products while serving multiple customers.
Consult with executive management to develop and implement current, annual, and long-term technical, schedule, quality, business, and financial objectives for the program(s), and contribute to the development of Group/Company objectives which have a long-range forecast projected to continue for multiple years.
Manage the establishment of design concepts, criteria, and engineering efforts for product research, development, testing, and integration.
Interact with senior management concerning matters of significance to the company and act as the primary contact for program issues.
Direct, influence, and coordinate the preparation of proposals, business plans, proposal work statements and specifications, operating budgets, and financial terms/conditions of contract(s); influence contract acquisitions, negotiations, and modifications.
Ensure technical leadership and excellence are maintained by directing and participating in the planning, attraction, selection, retention, and development of the required management, professional, and technical talent.
Act as the primary customer contact for program activities and lead program review sessions with customers to discuss cost, schedule, and technical performance.
Identify program issues and provide leadership in developing solutions such as re-allocation of resources or modifying contract specifications.
Lead the development of new business opportunities and expansion of existing business opportunities. Participate with Group management in pursuing business partnerships, alliances, and joint ventures that enhance the capabilities of the Group/Company and may result in new products, programs, and business opportunities.
Direct the development of and ensure the security of proprietary technology and maintain the strict confidentiality of sensitive information.
Other duties as assigned or required.

Leadership Characteristics:

Demonstrates strong ownership and accountability for program outcomes, including technical, schedule, quality, business, and financial performance.
Builds, leads, and develops high-performing cross-functional teams, including management, professional, and technical staff.
Effectively influences and aligns multiple stakeholders, including customers, suppliers, and internal organizations, around program and business objectives.
Communicates clearly, concisely, and transparently with executive leadership, customers, and team members on program status, risks, and opportunities.
Makes sound, timely decisions in a complex environment, balancing technical, business, and customer considerations.
Fosters a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and collaboration across programs and functions.
Demonstrates resilience and adaptability in managing change, resolving issues, and driving programs to successful completion.

We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals with diverse backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply.

Job Qualifications

Typically requires a Bachelor’s, Master’s or PhD in engineering, science or a related technical field as well as fifteen or more years of progressively complex program administration experience with at least nine of those years managing programs. May substitute equivalent experience in lieu of education.

Demonstrates detailed and extensive technical expertise and application of program management principles, concepts, and practice as well as comprehensive program management and leadership skills including organizing, planning, scheduling, and coordinating workloads to meet established deadlines or milestones. Must be able to develop solutions to complex problems that require the regular use of ingenuity and creativity.

Strong communication, leadership, presentation, and interpersonal skills are required to enable an effective interface with other departments, all levels of management, professional and support staff, customers, potential customers, and government representatives.

Active DoD Secret clearance is highly preferred. Candidates must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret clearance if not already held.

jobs.description:
Overview

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.

We are currently hiring a Development Director, School Engagement. This is a full time, field-based position that requires extensive travel across the Santa Clara County, Alameda,
and Santa Cruz
areas. Flexibility in working hours, including early mornings and evenings, is essential to accommodate the needs of schools and events.

In this fast-paced fundraising/sales position, you will engage K-12 students with the Kids Heart Challenge and American Heart Challenge, working with hundreds of schools to promote physical activity and learning. The role also involves extensive data management, continuously updating account information in our customer relationship management (CRM) databases and Microsoft Office products.

Combine your love for fundraising and sales with your passion for kids' health!

Monday - Friday, 8 am - 4:30 pm

Territory:
Bloomfield

At Hospice of New Jersey, we take immense pride in being a mission-driven, patient-centered leader in end-of-life care. Guided by our vision to be the most trusted partner in hospice care, we surround our patients and their loved ones with unwavering support, comfort, and compassion. At Hospice of New Jersey, we look for dedicated professionals who share our belief that true hospice care extends beyond medical needs—it’s about bringing dignity, peace, and human connection to every life we touch.

Comprehensive Health, Dental, & Vision Insurance

Responsibilities

Forge Strong Connections: Partner with our Liaisons to foster good working relations with physicians, hospitals, nursing facilities, and more. Together, we'll extend our reach and help even more people!
Build the Dream Team: Employ qualified colleagues and ensure adequate colleague orientation, training, education, and evaluation. Together, we'll grow and thrive!
Be the Backbone of Excellence: Organize and supervise the administrative functions of the hospice program and overall local operations. Your skills will keep us running smoothly!
Compliance Champion: Maintain compliance with applicable laws and regulations and implement corrective action if needed. Your attention to detail will keep us on the right track!

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
HFHA is currently seeking a dynamic Executive Director
who will serve as a strong visionary leader working in partnership with the Board of Directors to develop goals and strategies consistent with the vision, mission and values of HFHA. This position oversees all programs to ensure staffing and the financial capacity necessary to accomplish goals established by the Board of Directors and ensures compliance with reporting and regulatory requirements.

A successful candidate should demonstrate strong leadership; a collaborative working style; interpersonal and supervisory skills; keen business acumen; excellent judgment and instincts; a strong work ethic; a positive outlook; knowledge of seasonal project planning; a regard for strong community and cross-sector partnerships, including knowledge of Alaska nonprofit funding and relationship dynamics; and a bias for action. The candidate must be comfortable leading in a global, humanitarian, Christian-based organization and serving as the public face of HFHA.

BUDGET & FINANCE

Secure and steward diverse funding sources, including grants, private and corporate donors; oversee the preparation of grant applications and ensure accurate reporting, compliance, and tracking of all grant expenditures and outcomes.
Lead the collective work of the full Management Team to assure HFHA continues to operate a fiscally responsible annual budget with transparency.
In conjunction with the Board of Directors, facilitate the creation and implementation of annual budgets, goals and objectives.
Present reports on financial planning, status, anticipated problems and alternatives.
Establish appropriate accountability measures to achieve revenue targets at HFHA’s ReStore retail operation.
Responsible for fiscal management that generally anticipates operating within the approved budget, ensuring maximum resource utilization, and maintenance of the organization in a positive financial position.

OPERATIONS & PROGRAM MANAGEMENT

Manage day-to-day operations of the organization ensuring that all facets of the organization efficiently and effectively fulfill the mission of HFHA.
Translate plans into operational actions with measurable results and clear accountability.
Ensure official records, documents, policies and procedures are compliant with federal, state and local regulations and Habitat for Humanity International standards.
Engage external organizations and communities to understand significant developments and trends in the area of safe, affordable housing.
Support the promotion, growth, and purpose of the ReStore retail operation.

COMMUNICATIONS & PUBLIC RELATIONS

Serve as a visible ambassador for HFHA, promoting its programs, impact, and goals to maintain a strong, positive public image.
Establish and leverage strong, collaborative relationships with federal, state, and municipal agencies; community organizations; investors and donors; other affordable housing providers; and key partners essential to advancing HFHA’s mission.
Lead engagement with Alaska-specific funding sources, including state and municipal programs, private foundations, and Alaska Native corporations and organizations.
Establish a deliberate, comprehensive advocacy program that identifies key issues, opportunities and stakeholders.

HUMAN RESOURCES

Determine staffing and capacity needs of HFHA including employees and volunteers.
Manage employee relations including recruitment, professional development, evaluation, corrective action, and compliance.
Encourage staff and volunteer development and education.
Maintain a climate which attracts, keeps, and motivates a diverse staff.
Provide inspirational leadership and direction, developing leaders within the organization.

BOARD RELATIONS

Cultivate a strong, diverse, inclusive and highly engaged Board.
Assist the Board in strategic planning and advise on issues affecting HFHA’s mission.
Ensure effective board relations through regular communication.

General Skills & Qualifications

Understand and support HFHA’s purpose, vision and values
Minimum five (5) years of leadership experience
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
Demonstrated ability to prepare and administer budgets
Development and fundraising experience
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Strong relationship-building and collaboration skills
Ability to manage competing priorities under pressure
Resilient, energetic, collaborative, and flexible leadership style
Willingness to be actively engaged in Alaska for funding and housing resources

Preferred Skills & Qualifications

Prior executive leadership within Habitat for Humanity or housing-focused nonprofits
Experience with Alaska’s leadership in nonprofit and funding ecosystem
Established relationships with Alaska-based funders including the Rasmuson Foundation and Alaska Native entities
Experience with earned revenue operations
Background in affordable housing, community development, or advocacy
Experience managing complex organizations and compliance environments
Master’s degree in a related field

jobs.description:
Reports To: Vice President of Operations

Registered Nurse Licensure Required for this role.

About Luminary Hospice:

At Luminary Hospice, we are a mission-driven organization that empowers our team members to shape our culture in order to allow them to provide the highest quality support to patients and families throughout their entire end-of-life journey.

Our mission is to deliver personalized care that radiates compassion and preserves dignity for all that we are honored to serve on their end-of-life journey. We are centered on caring for the whole person – with expert medical care, pain management as well as emotional and spiritual support along with resources, information, and emotional support for families and caregivers.

About the role:

The Executive Director/Administrator is responsible for the overall direction of the hospice services.  He/she is responsible for the employment of qualified hospice personnel; is responsible for the provision of hospice services, directly, and the delegation to and coordination of hospice personnel evaluations; is responsible for establishing standards of care to comply with federal and state regulations and guidelines.  The Executive Director/Administrator establishes, implements, and evaluates goals and objectives for hospice services that meet and promote the standards of quality and contribute to the total organization and philosophy.    

Job Responsibilities:

Operational planning and budgeting. 
Ensuring organizational compliance with legal, regulatory, and accreditation requirements. 
Assures that all business conduct is above minimum standards required by law and will not condone any activities that achieve results through violation of the law, unethical business, or patient care practices. 
Monitoring business operations to ensure financial stability. 
Evaluating hospice services and personnel using measurable outcomes and objectives. 
Conflict and complaint management and resolution. 
Establishing and maintaining effective channels of communication including integration or technology, as applicable. 
Ensuring hospice personnel stay current with clinical information and practices. 
Ensuring adequate and appropriate staffing. 
Staff development including orientation, in-service, continuing education, competency testing, and quality assessment performance improvement. 
Ensuring that interdisciplinary care is provided. 
Ensuring supportive services are available to personnel. 
Ensuring coordination with other departments, services, and senior management, as appropriate. 
Ensuring staff and organization stay current on local and national hospice issues and trends. 
Ensuring that appropriate service policies and procedures are developed and implemented to accomplish identified outcomes. 
Directing staff in the performance of their duties including admission, discharge, transfer, revocation, and provision of service to patients. 
Ensuring appropriate staff supervision during all service hours. 
Monitoring service utilization to ensure delivery of comprehensive care. 
Ensuring services provided by other agencies are authorized by the hospice. 
Monitoring operational progress toward accomplishing operational and strategic goals.  
Ensuring appropriate data collection and regular, complete reports are received by the Governing Body. 
Ensuring adequate space, equipment, and supplies are available. 
Ensuring actionable objectives are derived from the evaluation of hospice services and personnel. 
Ensuring that structure and systems promote interdisciplinary care 
Ensuring collaboration with agencies and vendors for effective management of services. 
Ensuring standards of ethical business and clinical practice are maintained    

The above statements are intended to be a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job.  The incumbents may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those stated in this description. 

Job Qualifications:

Registered Nurse licensure required
Two (2) to five (5) years experience in health care management. 
Demonstrates an ability to supervise and direct professional and administrative personnel. 
Has an ability to deal tactfully with the community. 
Knows corporate business management. 
Understands hospice care and the services provided to patients and family/caregivers through an interdisciplinary group.  I
Intimate knowledge of Medicare Hospice Certification.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit or stand. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

All employment decisions at Luminary Hospice are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications.

3 years minimum prior relevant experience and at least 1 year of supervisory experience.

Consistent track record in exceeding sales/fundraising goals.
Experience in recruiting, training, and advising multiple staff in a team environment.
Understand and navigate workplace cultures to achieve goals.
Proven experience in building powerful partnerships with corporate leaders and senior-level volunteers; interact and communicate clearly and concisely, exchange ideas, facts, and information.

Display outstanding organizational, communication, negotiation, and social skills.
Outstanding written and oral communication skills, including large and small group presentations.
Proficiency in identifying and addressing challenges.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Director of Operations

Reports to: Vice President, Direct Cash Transfers

Start Date: October 1, 2026

Salary range: $120,000 to $135,000

Overview

Point Source Youth (PSY) is a national leader in the movement to prevent and end youth homelessness with a planned annual budget of over $7 million dollars. Founded in 2015, we partner with communities to scale direct cash transfers as prevention, our Targeted Housing Assistance Program, and a 24-month Direct Cash Transfers for housing program, as well as other evidence-based strategies that center the agency of young people, especially BIPOC and LGBTQIA2S+ youth, to prevent and end youth homelessness. Our work includes research, policy, advocacy, fundraising, storytelling, movement building, narrative change, and implementation, culminating each year in our National Symposium on Solutions to End Youth Homelessness.

We seek an experienced collaborative, detail-oriented, and strategic leader to serve as our Director of Operations. The Director of Operations will lead PSY’s next stage of growth, with a strong emphasis on strengthening the organization’s infrastructure and building a culture of excellence, compliance, and effective risk management.

As the leader of the organization's human resources function and day-to-day operations, this role oversees the full employee lifecycle, state compliance, required filings, internal communications, administrative systems, and basic financial planning. The ideal candidate brings a systems-oriented approach, exceptional attention to detail, and a strong problem-solving skill set to support staff well-being and organizational growth. They will champion a culture centered on excellence, compliance, and risk management, ensuring that internal infrastructure keeps pace with our mission. By managing complex workflows and building robust organizational systems, they will ensure our work is stronger, compliant, more equitable, and highly effective.

Responsibilities

Human Resources Leadership & People Operations (30%)

• Lead all core HR activities for the organization, serving as the primary owner of HR strategy, policy, and day-to-day administration.
• Lead onboarding for all new hires, ensuring a consistent, compliant, and welcoming experience from offer through the first 90 days as well as leading a quarterly and annual review process.
• Support performance management cycles, staff development processes, and implementation of effective HR practices.
• Lead PSY’s HR matters and create a thoughtful and supportive culture in order to meet our goals and mission.
• Assist with benefits administration, including enrollments, eligibility tracking, and liaison with our PEO.
• Lead employee off-boarding processes, including documentation, exit interviews, final pay compliance, and benefits off-boarding, in accordance with applicable employment law.
• Maintain accurate and confidential HR records, ensuring compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws.
• Support the completion and maintenance of all required state filings and registrations related to employment, including multi-state employer registrations, unemployment insurance, and workers' compensation.
• Ensure ongoing state-by-state compliance in conjunction with the PEO.
• Serve as the organization's primary administrator of ADP, managing payroll coordination with our accounting team, employee records, benefits administration, and reporting.
• Determine how the PEO should be best utilized by the organization.
• Lead timesheet process and communication, including and communications with the PEO.
• Support staff development processes to achieve organizational goals and ensure compliance and risk management processes are implemented and managed to the highest standards
• Ensure ongoing compliance with required staff trainings (e.g., cybersecurity training, sexual harassment training) and recommend and create expanded training programs
• Update and maintain operations and employee manuals.

Organizational Operations & Systems Management (30%)

• Oversee and continually improve internal operations across teams, ensuring workflows are efficient and aligned with organizational priorities.
• Develop and maintain organizational policies, procedures, and Standard Operating Procedures to ensure consistency, compliance, and operational clarity.
• Manage vendor relationships, technology systems, facilities coordination, and organizational subscriptions.
• Manage the creation, execution, and ongoing maintenance of all contracts and Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with partners and consultants.
• Track and report on operational performance metrics; provide regular updates to executive leadership.
• Lead organizational risk management processes, including compliance with nonprofit regulations, insurance updates, annual filings, and the creation of a staff training program.
• Support cross-departmental projects by ensuring clear timelines, documentation, and communication pathways.
• Initiate and facilitate trainings to ensure compliance excellence, risk management, and goal completion
• Oversee all administrative and home office purchases.
• Support annual audit and tax filings by acting as a liaison between management, the Board, and the outsourced team for all required information and documents.
Lead annual insurance renewal process for the organization's insurance needs
Lead the organization's IT and cyber security risk management processes working with an external IT partner
Develop and implement the organization’s AI policy

Finance Support & Administrative Stewardship (30%)

• Support leadership with preparation of the annual organizational budget and lead forecasting.
• Track expenses and monitor department spending.
• Lead financial forecasting of profit and loss analysis on projects and create a process for financial forecasting for future years .
• Submit regular invoices to external parties as needed.
• Process invoices using Bill.com; train consultants and staff on the platform and provide guides and tools as needed.
• Maintain financial documentation and assist with audit preparation, grant reporting materials, and compliance requirements.
• Collaborate closely with the external accounting firm to ensure accurate bookkeeping and financial reporting.
• Track restricted and unrestricted funds in partnership with program and finance staff to ensure proper allocation.
• Manage annual filings for state compliance with an outsourced team.
Internal and External Communication & Cross-Functional Collaboration (10%)

• Maintain and organize records and administrative documentation using platforms such as Google Drive, Slack, ADP, and Toggl.
• Engage in internal working groups, strategic planning initiatives, and team culture development activities.
• Provide scheduling support to leadership for both internal and external meetings.
• Provide support for our Annual National Symposium on Solutions to End Youth Homelessness
• Other tasks as assigned.

Qualifications

• Minimum of 7-12 years of progressive experience in nonprofit operations, HR leadership, or organizational management, including direct experience leading onboarding and terminations.
• Significant experience working directly with executive leadership including executive director, CEO, or president.
• Demonstrated experience managing state filings and registrations for a multi-state employer.
• Proficiency as a PEO is required.
• Experience with BambooHR is a plus.
• Strong understanding of nonprofit operational requirements, financial structures, compliance, and HR best practices.
• Strong working knowledge of federal and state employment law (FLSA, FMLA, EEO, state-specific requirements, etc.).
• Demonstrated experience implementing or improving organizational systems, workflows, and administrative tools.
• Proven ability to manage budgets, track financial data, and coordinate with accounting or financial partners.
Demonstrated experience overseeing IT system and IT security processes

• Exceptional organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
• Demonstrated commitment to equity.
• Ability to travel for team meetings, conferences, or partner engagements.
• Proven ability to manage confidential information and operate at the highest levels of discretion.
• Excellent project management and organizational skills.
• Ideally, experience with BambooHR, Salesforce, Toggl and time tracking, and Bill.com.
• Will work 9 AM-5 PM Eastern Standard Time.

At this point in your career, your #1 priority is to join a fully remote company that prioritizes flexibility in the workplace, and that promotes a culture of respect, kindness, and transparency. Solution driven!

jobs.title: Associate Vice President of Development
jobs.description:
Overview

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.

The American Heart Association has an excellent opportunity for an Associate Vice President, Development
(AVP) in the Boston metro market.

In this position, responsibilities include leading a revenue-driving team and partnering with corporations, C-suite leaders, and philanthropists to drive fundraising efforts for the Boston Social campaigns, including the Heart & Stroke Gala and Go Red For Women Luncheon,
and contributing $2M to the overall market goal.

Additionally, responsibilities include expanding year-round support for the Luncheon and Gala campaigns, a key priority is to grow the STEM Goes Red initiative, along with the Women and Teen of Impact campaigns. Accountable for revenue generation and corporate development activities as well as handling top corporate accounts, securing cause sponsorships, identifying and recruiting volunteer leadership, recruiting Executive Leadership Teams, and holding others accountable to the team fundraising goals and objectives. We’re looking for a proactive individual who enjoys taking initiative and is excited to lead and support our team.

This office-based role, with a hybrid work schedule, requires approximately 75% travel within the assigned territory. In this fast-paced environment, the position plays a critical role in driving revenue to support our mission. The role is based in our Wellesley, MA office.

We offer a base salary with the potential to earn an incentive up to 25% of your base pay. The potential incentive is based on achieving certain revenue targets and triggers.

The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. To help you be successful, you will have access to Heart U, our award-winning corporate university, as well as additional training and support, locally.

\#TheAHALife is more than a company culture; it is our way of life. It embodies our commitment to work-life harmonization and is guided by our core values where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally. Discover why you will Be Seen. Be Heard. Be Valued at the American Heart Association by following us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs.

Responsibilities

The Associate Vice President will plan, coordinate, staff, and lead the Greater Boston market’s operations for the Heart & Stroke Gala and Go Red for Women campaign initiatives to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of fundraising efforts. Will work closely with the Vice President, Development, along with internal and external partners to ensure unified health and revenue efforts for the campaigns, and will serve in a player/coach capacity.

Guide and direct assigned staff to reach fundraising goals. Accountable for hiring, directing, training, evaluating, and coaching staff under their supervision.
Ensuring your team meets/exceeds annual revenue goals for the market.
Engage, recruit, and mobilize CEOs, corporate leaders, and community leaders to serve on each of the campaign's leadership committees and to chair the event, ensuring fundraising and health outcomes success. This includes encouraging personal and corporate giving of volunteer leaders.
Lead existing and new sponsorships and relationships to achieve campaign goals through the cultivation, stewardship, renewal, and deepening engagement via frequent face-to-face meetings to retain and upgrade their financial dedication, according to each campaign's timeline and business plan.
Lead coordinated planning processes for the Gala and Go Red for Women’s health and revenue efforts for all functional areas. Actively involve, inform, and integrate with internal partners across the metro market, region, and association.
Research, identify, and acquire companies to support the campaigns. Empower employers to establish recruitment and monetary goals based on market potential and their role in achieving goals.
Develop and lead/monitor each campaign's budget within the span of control and in accordance with internal business operations, policies, and fiscal standards, and in accordance with the approved operating budget.
Prepares plans, documents, and communications for GAP (getting to goal) meetings, revenue projection updates, and other priority meetings as they arise.
Coordinate with business operations to provide a seamless donor and participant experience through event logistics excellence.
Willingness to continuously learn about the organization's standard methodologies with dedication to implementation.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to implement market strategies, build blended sponsorships, and relationships with volunteers and other campaigns.

Qualifications

Want to help get your resume to the top? Take a look at the experience we require:

University/College degree or equivalent experience.
3 years minimum prior relevant experience and at least 1 year of supervisory experience.
Strong experience in individual giving and corporate fundraising preferred.
Consistent track record in exceeding sales/fundraising goals.
Experience in recruiting, training, and advising multiple staff in a team environment.
Understand and navigate workplace cultures to achieve goals.
Proven experience in building powerful partnerships with corporate leaders and senior-level volunteers; interact and communicate clearly and concisely, exchange ideas, facts, and information.
Proven track record of cultivating major donors, securing city-wide sponsorships, and recruiting new companies and donors.
Direct knowledge of special event fundraising tactics is essential.
Display outstanding organizational, communication, negotiation, and social skills.
Outstanding written and oral communication skills, including large and small group presentations.
Proficiency in identifying and addressing challenges.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to do daily local travel up to 75%; requires access to reliable transportation at all times on an immediate basis.

Compensation & Benefits

The expected pay range will be $88,320 to $117,875. Pay is commensurate with experience; geographic differentials to the pay range may apply. American Heart Association reserves the right to pay more or less than the posted range. This position is incentive-eligible based on achieving certain targets.

The American Heart Association invests in its people. Here are the main components of our total rewards package. Visit Rewards & Benefits to see more details.

Compensation – Our goal is to ensure you have a competitive base salary. That’s why we regularly review the market value of jobs and make adjustments, as needed.
Performance and Recognition – You are rewarded for achieving success through annual salary planning and incentive programs; this position is incentive eligible based on achieving certain targets.
Benefits – We offer a wide array of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, along with a robust retirement program that includes an employer match and automatic contribution. As a mark of our commitment to employee well-being, we also offer an employee assistance program, employee wellness program and telemedicine, and medical consultation.
Professional Development – You can join one of our many Employee Resource Groups (ERG) or be a mentor/mentee in our professional mentoring program. Heart U is the Association’s national online university, with more than 100,000 resources designed to meet your needs and busy schedule.
Work-Life Harmonization – The Association offers Paid Time Off (PTO) at a minimum of 16 days per year for new employees. The number of days will increase based on seniority level. You will also have a total of 12 paid holidays off each year, which includes several days off at the end of the year.
Tuition Assistance - We support the career development of all employees. This program provides financial assistance to employees who wish to further their education and career in relation to their current duties and responsibilities, or for potential future positions in the organization.

Description

Title: Development Director

Position Status: Full-time, exempt

Reports to: CEO

OPPORTUNITY

Palo Alto Humane has spent more than a century championing the human-animal bond — and we're at an inflection point. Our programs are growing, our community presence is deepening, and we're ready to build the fundraising infrastructure to match our ambition.

This is a rare opportunity for a fundraiser who wants to own something. You won't be inheriting a rigid system or managing a large team — you'll be the architect of our development function, with direct access to leadership, a board that's engaged and ready to open doors, and a mission that resonates deeply with donors in one of the most philanthropically active regions in the country.

If you're energized by the idea of building something that lasts — a donor community, a major gifts pipeline, a culture of philanthropy — and you want your work to have a direct, visible impact on animals and the people who love them, we'd love to meet you.

ORGANIZATION

Palo Alto Humane’s mission is to inspire our community to connect humanely with animals. We believe in the transformative bond between humans and animals and aim to support both. We are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, charitable, volunteer-supported organization, and one of the few humane societies nationwide with no animal shelter.

Our programs and services ensure pets remain in homes with their families, support spay/neuter efforts across Santa Clara County and provide experiences for people to connect with friendly pets when they may not have a pet of their own. For more than a century PAH’s focus has been to alleviate the suffering of animals, increase public sensitivity to animal issues and elevate the status of animals in our society.

POSITION DETAILS

As our dedicated Development Director, you'll lead all fundraising strategy and execution — from major gifts and donor stewardship to solicitations and the Charity Checkout program. You'll report directly to the CEO and work closely with our board and small team to build PAH's development function from the ground up.

Key Responsibilities

Fundraising Strategy & Donor Relations

Design and lead PAH's comprehensive fundraising strategy — spanning major gifts, annual campaigns, recurring donors, donor advised funds, planned giving, giving platforms, and written solicitations.
Set annual and multi-year fundraising goals and budgets in partnership with the CEO.
Identify, cultivate and steward major donors, corporate partners, and legacy sponsors alongside the CEO.
Oversee donor stewardship and recognition – ensuring acknowledgements, tax receipts, and creative recognition ideas reflect fundraising best practices.
Maintain the donor database, ensuring accurate records and meaningful donor engagement.
Develop engagement plans for stock giving and donor advised fund giving.
Build and grow the “Charity Checkout” program, our point-of-sale giving initiative with local veterinary practices and businesses.

Communications & Marketing

Partner with the Director of Community Engagement (and Marketing Consultant) to create stories and content across social media, email solicitations and communications, newsletters annual reports, and press releases that bring PAH’s mission and impact to life.
Help grow PAH’s digital presence, including our website and social channels.

Organizational Leadership & Reporting

Provide regular fundraising updates to the Board and leadership team.
Set key performance indicators (KPIs) for fundraising and marketing efforts, using real-time data to refine strategy. Help build a culture of philanthropy across PAH - coaching staff, board members, and volunteers on fundraising.
Engage in ongoing professional development and goal-setting with the CEO.

As a small team, we all wear multiple hats — we're looking for someone who sees that as an opportunity, not a constraint.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 90 days, you'll get to know PAH from the inside out — meeting with the CEO, board, and staff, auditing our current donor database and fundraising materials, and building relationships with our key supporters. By the end of this period, you'll have a clear picture of where we stand and draft a roadmap for the year ahead.

By the end of year one, you'll have launched at least one new fundraising initiative or strengthened an existing program (such as a robust DAF program, a major gifts pipeline, or an extensive Charity Checkout program). In addition, you will have established KPIs that give leadership and the board real visibility into fundraising performance, and built the early foundation of a donor stewardship system that will support PAH's growth for years to come.

Qualifications

Passion for PAH’s mission, vision and core values.
Minimum of five years of fundraising experience in the nonprofit sector, and a college degree or extensive experience in relationship management roles (private foundations, sales, financial advising, etc.).
Proven success developing and executing fundraising initiatives.
Experience cultivating, soliciting and stewarding individual donors.
Exposure to major gifts work or program, or experience managing a donor portfolio desired.
Demonstrated ability to increase revenue and ensure long-term strategic growth.
Self-starter with the ability to drive projects to completion with minimal supervision.
Strong problem-solver and critical thinker, ability to synthesize data and make evidence-based decisions.
Persuasive and clear communicator with excellent organizational, written, verbal and interpersonal skills.
Proficiency in DonorPerfect (or similar donor software platforms such as Blackbaud or Salesforce), Constant Contact, Google Workspace, Microsoft Suite, Canva, VistaPrint, and digital marketing tools.

Salary/Compensation

Salary of $85-90k + bonuses based on meeting mutually agreed upon fundraising revenue and donor targets.

Benefits

Annual $1000 pet care benefit - because we mean it when we say animals are family
Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance.
Accrual-based PTO (up to 10 days in first year of employment with annual increases based on years of service).
Partial remote/hybrid flexibility.
Flexible work-week scheduling.
Three paid sick days annually.
Eight paid holidays.
Professional development or training opportunities with Board approval.

ACCESSIBILITY AND ACCOMMODATIONS

Role requires prolonged periods of sitting and extensive use of a computer, including typing and screen time.
Must be able to communicate effectively via email, video calls, and other digital communication tools.
Must have flexibility to work occasional weekends and evenings.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Please submit cover letter and resume to Robert Armbrust, at ceo@paloaltohumane.org.

jobs.description:
Iconic Adventures is hiring a senior account leader and trusted travel expert (“Client Engagement Director”) to lead complex travel planning for key partnerships and client relationships. This is an individual contributor role with substantial leadership responsibility. We are looking for someone with the poise and expertise to steward and grow client relationships, and the global destination knowledge and operational depth to execute on their own vision.

Our portfolio spans donor and impact travel, corporate and affinity groups, global charity challenge events, and luxury FIT experiences. Luxury FIT and international expertise is required for this hiring round;
experience across other segments is a plus. (If you meet all qualifications except luxury/FIT background, please indicate this at the top of your cover letter, and we will hold your resume for future consideration.)

Key Responsibilities

Trip Design and Development

Own the design and development of your itineraries end to end, from first concept through final program execution and budget reconciliation.
Bring first-hand destination expertise and supplier judgment to every itinerary, drawing on where you have traveled, guided, or operated.
Set the vision and the standard for each trip project, and direct the development process that Trip Development Managers and Coordinators support you in executing. 
Select and negotiate contracting with ground operators, lodges, and specialty suppliers.
Stay current on destinations, properties, and operators in your business area.

Client Management and Strategic Partnership

Build consultative, long-term relationships with your private (B2C) and organizational (B2B) clients across design, sales, and delivery. Act as a trusted advisor and treat clients as valued partners.
Present and sell itineraries directly, addressing highlights and tradeoffs with tact and clarity.
Act as a liaison between stakeholders, identifying decision-makers within groups or organizations and surfacing solutions.
Uphold discretion and confidentiality, safeguarding client privacy at all times.
Maintain a big-picture perspective on the client’s goals and be proactive in identifying growth opportunities for the partnership, with a client-first mindset.

Proposals, Budgets, and Forecasting

Build and present compelling itinerary and program proposals.
Develop and manage complex trip budgets across the full lifecycle, owning pricing assumptions, margin targets, and post-trip reconciliation.
Forecast revenue and margin across your portfolio and surface variances early.

Project Management 

Align trip planning with the client’s mission, values, internal structures, and approval processes.
Oversee projects with multiple stakeholders: clients, travelers, local partners, and internal teams.
Manage expectations and control scope by aligning on deliverables and clearly communicating the implications of timeline or project changes.
Anticipate and address client needs proactively and strategically.
Manage planning challenges with diplomacy and sensitivity.
Communicate clearly and concisely with stakeholders to align expectations and logistics.

What You Will Bring

Required

8+ years of progressive experience within trip development and the travel industry, with a substantial portion of that spent designing and developing itineraries yourself.
Expertise with international destinations and high-touch travel. You are well-traveled and fluent in the bespoke market.
Demonstrated ability to manage clients, customers and complex programs, including the ability to lead cross-functional teams without formal authority.
Demonstrated ownership of itineraries from concept through delivery.
Proven ownership of complex trip budgets across the full lifecycle.
Experience building and presenting client proposals that won or renewed business.
Excellent written and verbal communication paired with strong presentation and negotiation skills.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.

Preferred

Guiding or trip-leading experience.
People or team management experience.
Client presentation and travel conference experience.
Event management background.
Spanish language proficiency; other languages are a plus.

How You Work

You lead through judgment, influence, and credibility, whether or not you formally manage the people supporting your work.
You are a doer. You are as comfortable building an itinerary yourself as you are directing a team to build it, and you know when each is called for.
You are tech-forward and systems-oriented. You adopt tools quickly and use AI tools thoughtfully in your administrative workflow. AI does not inspire or guide your trip design.
You are extremely thorough. You elevate structure and take delight in organization. 
You are kind. Even better, you have a sense of humor and grow from your mistakes.
You handle difficult conversations directly and hold scope without damaging the relationship.
You work effectively in a remote environment, with flexibility for the occasional evening or weekend tied to live itineraries running in the field.

What We Bring to the Table

Access to an incredible global network of suppliers, including DMCs and hotels, vetted partners, professional industry networks, and field staff to help you build your client’s dream trip.
Trip development support that scales with your client portfolio.
A dynamic environment with the technology and tools to do your best work.
A path to growing your career in the travel industry. Iconic Adventures has a growing portfolio of sister companies and clients across private, corporate, and nonprofit travel. Join us for an exciting new phase of opportunity and partnership!

Benefits

Health and dental coverage.
Unlimited PTO.
401(k) plan with employer match.
Paid parental leave.
FAM opportunities.
An annual discretionary allowance to support your working environment.
An annual company retreat to reset and connect with colleagues.
Optional use of our Steamboat Springs, Colorado office.

Employment Terms

Hiring Process and What to Expect

Due to the volume of interest, we are not able to respond to every application, but we read each one.

Apply through the Iconic Adventures BambooHR job posting by submitting a resume and cover letter. https://iconicadventure.bamboohr.com/careers/28

jobs.description:
MHW Search
has exclusively partnered with a well-established retail investment/development firm in Houston in search of a Director of Development.

THE PLATFORM

Our client is a privately held, vertically integrated commercial real estate investment and development firm with in-house capabilities spanning development, construction, brokerage, leasing, and property management.

The company specializes in the development of neighborhood retail centers, grocery-anchored shopping centers, single-tenant build-to-suit projects, and pad-site developments within high-growth markets across Texas and Florida. Through an integrated operating platform, the firm delivers projects from initial site acquisition through development, leasing, disposition, and long-term asset management.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Our client is seeking a Director of Development
to lead build-to-suit and single-tenant development projects from initial site identification through stabilization and disposition. This is a principal-level development role with full lifecycle ownership.

The successful candidate will originate tenant relationships and requirements, source and control development sites, underwrite and structure transactions, negotiate land contracts, oversee due diligence, manage entitlements and permitting, coordinate construction and financing activities, deliver completed projects to tenants, and ultimately guide each asset through stabilization and disposition. Accountability spans the entire development lifecycle, with responsibility for the overall success of each project rather than a single phase.

This position supports two primary business channels. The first involves managing programmatic relationships with regional and national tenants executing multi-unit development programs. In these assignments, the Director serves as the primary point of contact and is responsible for delivering consistent underwriting discipline, schedule execution, communication, and development quality across multiple markets. The second consists of one-off build-to-suit and reverse build-to-suit developments, as well as the single-tenant and pad-site components of larger mixed-use and multi-tenant projects.

The firm operates as a merchant developer, underwriting projects toward defined investment returns and disposition objectives. Success is measured not only by delivering high-quality developments, but by achieving or exceeding the project's targeted financial performance.
This role has also been intentionally designed around technology and operational efficiency. Managing sourcing, entitlements, capital coordination, construction oversight, and dispositions across multiple concurrent developments requires an individual who has fundamentally modernized their development process. Extensive, demonstrable proficiency utilizing artificial intelligence to improve workflow, analysis, documentation, and project execution is considered a core requirement of this position.

REPORTING & STRUCTURE

Reports directly to executive leadership within the Development division.

jobs.title: Director of Operations, Health Analytics Practice
jobs.description:
We do Consulting Differently

BRG Healthcare supports life sciences companies, payors, providers and their legal teams facing high-stakes investigations and disputes, complex regulations, evolving payment models, and fragmented data systems. Our team provides innovative data analytics, economic and financial modeling, forensic analysis, and expert testimony specialized for the unique details and pressures of the healthcare industry.

About The Opportunity

The Director of Operations, Health Analytics Practice will report to the Health Analytics Practice (HAP) Executive Leadership team. The HAP team needs a strategic player with an entrepreneurial mindset who can thrive in ambiguity. HAP falls under the umbrella of the firm’s wider ISP (Industries & Special Practices) Community.

This position is based in Chicago, New York, Washington, DC, or Tampa.

This position requires a self-motivated individual with strong communication, leadership, organizational, strategic, and financial analysis skills who can:

Work with HAP experts and senior staff to drive practice strategy, improved financial performance, and growth in revenue and profitability.
Collaborate with BRG’s Financial Planning & Analytics (FP&A) team and HAP leadership to maintain and utilize rolling tracking and forecasting tools to drive financial performance at the practice/expert level, including efforts to achieve revenue, margins, utilization, leverage, and other goals based on key indicators. Collaborate with FP&A to monitor HAP financial performance and work with HAP experts to schedule periodic check-ins with financial performance updates.
Act as a liaison between HAP leadership, the ISP community’s Director of Operations, and critical corporate VPs responsible for expert performance review, cross-community staffing and utilization, compensation, and staff performance review and management.
Lead strategic practice initiatives with guidance from HAP leadership, including staffing and utilization management, headcount forecasting, staff performance management, staff learning and development, and practice data management.
Work with HAP leadership to maintain and track various business development budgets and requests for funding.
Work with BRG Business Development professionals across the firm to develop, track, and coordinate BD opportunities, including job pitches, new case opportunities, and marketing events. Develop, support, and coordinate any cross-practice market facing initiatives.
Continue to improve internal communication efforts by working with HAP leadership to describe the practice’s progress and vision to success and growth to all practice members.
Assist in other aspects of practice support as identified by HAP leadership, including preparing meeting agendas, presentations, and updates for the firm’s leadership team and board.
Participate in planning HAP-related activities at the firm’s Managing Director summit and other HAP meetings.
Manage other operational individuals, such as HAP operations managers and ISP operations coordinators.

Expert and Staff Management Liaison

For junior and senior HAP staff, coordinate with HAP leadership and HR for onboarding, utilization management, annual performance management, compensation and bill rate increase processes, and coordinate with the ISP community’s Director of Operations to ensure appropriate level of consistency across the ISP community.
Coordinate with HAP leadership and the ISP community’s Director of Operations regarding staffing needs, utilization, and opportunities to cross-staff resources.
Coordinate with the ISP community’s campus and experienced staff recruiters to support talent pipeline, identify staffing needs, and determine the proper levels of recruiting team resources.
Coordinate with VP of Expert Relations related to expert onboarding and performance management.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate is a consultant or former consultant looking to move into a practice operations leadership role, who has a strategy, management, or finance background in a professional services firm.  Strong problem-solving skills, an entrepreneurial frame of mind, and an ability to drive internal projects independently are all desired.

Specific Skills And Experience Should Include

Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree, MBA, CFA, or CPA a plus
Minimum of 10 years of prior work experience, preferably in a fast-paced consulting environment
Ability to analyze financial information and build financial models for practice management initiatives (e.g., practice profitability, resource planning, compensation modeling, etc.)
Entrepreneurial mindset, with ability to problem solve and think independently and outside-the-box. Excellent written and oral communication skills with a confident and clear communication style
Aptitude to develop insights and recommendations to business problems
Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize changing work demands, and learn quickly
Mature presence, empathy, and intellectual curiosity
Demonstrate strong project management, time management, and organizational skills
Handle sensitive information and preserve its confidentiality
Strong understanding of managing relationships and developing solution-based proposals in a professional services environment
Expert working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Ability to travel, primarily to offices with significant presence of HAP staff including Boston, Chicago, New York, Tampa, and Washington, DC

Salary Range: 175k - 250k per year

Candidate must be able to submit verification of his/her legal right to work in the U.S., without company sponsorship.

About BRG

BRG combines world-leading academic credentials with world-tested business expertise and purpose-built emerging technologies. Our culture centers on agility and connectivity which sets us apart and gets you ahead.

At BRG, our professionals include specialist consultants, industry experts, renowned academics, and leading-edge data scientists. Together, they bring a diversity of real-world experience, data, and human and artificial intelligence, to economics, disputes, and investigations; corporate finance; and performance improvement services that address the most complex challenges facing organizations across the globe.

Our unique structure nurtures the interdisciplinary relationships that give us the edge, laying the groundwork for more informed insights and more original, incisive thinking. When paired with our global reach and resources, our diverse perspectives and technical capabilities make us uniquely capable to address our clients’ challenges. We get results because we know how to apply our thinking to your world.

At BRG, we don’t just show you what’s possible. We’re built to help you make it happen.

BRG is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Our hiring practices provide equal opportunity for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, gender, national origin, age, United States military veteran status, ancestry, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, medical condition including genetic characteristics or information, veteran status, or mental or physical disability so long as the essential functions of the job can be performed with or without reasonable accommodation, or any other protected category under federal, state, or local law.

Company Description
The Ivan and Mike Team is a top-ranked real estate group in South Florida, specializing in luxury residential and new development markets with concierge-level service and deep local expertise. Recognized among the top teams in Miami by outlets such as The Wall Street Journal, the team holds leading positions in new construction sales and ultra-wealthy broker networks, with over $2B+ in sales.

We leverage strong relationships with developers, an elite investor network, and a dedicated operations function to deliver exclusive pre-construction opportunities and high-profile transactions. Founded in 2015 by Ivan Chorney and Michael Martirena, the team has grown to 10+ agents and operations professionals with diverse backgrounds in sports, fashion, and tech, and serves a global clientele in multiple languages.

Based in Miami’s thriving luxury real estate market, the team focuses on helping clients capitalize on the region’s dynamic growth and world-class lifestyle.

About the Opportunity

We are seeking an exceptional Director of Operations to serve as the operational leader of the Ivan & Mike Team. This role is responsible for building, optimizing, and scaling the systems, technology, people, and processes that power one of South Florida's leading luxury real estate teams. The successful candidate will enable the founders to spend more time advising clients, winning listings, developing strategic relationships, and growing the business while ensuring operational excellence across every department.

Mission

Build and continuously improve the operating system of the business so the team can scale efficiently while delivering an exceptional luxury client experience.

Key Responsibilities

• Own and improve operational systems across listings, transactions, marketing, client service, finance, recruiting, and administration.
• Develop KPIs and executive dashboards to measure performance.
• Lead workflow optimization, SOP documentation, and accountability systems.
• Research and implement AI tools and automation to improve efficiency and client experience.
• Oversee CRM adoption, technology stack, vendor relationships, and operational budgets.
• Hire, onboard, coach, and develop operations personnel.
• Identify opportunities to improve profitability through automation, vendor management, and process improvements.
• Proactively identify bottlenecks and recommend better ways of operating.

What Success Looks Like in the First 12 Months

• Streamlined operational workflows across the business.
• Real-time KPI dashboards supporting leadership decisions.
• Increased adoption of technology and AI automations.
• Improved hiring, onboarding, and accountability systems.
• Reduced operational bottlenecks and enhanced client experience.
• Ivan & Mike spending significantly more time on revenue-generating activities.

Qualifications

• 5+ years leading operations in luxury real estate, hospitality, consulting, professional services, or another high-touch business.
• Proven experience building scalable systems and improving organizational efficiency.
• Strong leadership, project management, analytical, and communication skills.
• Highly organized, proactive, data-driven, and comfortable leveraging modern technology and AI.
• Entrepreneurial mindset with a continuous-improvement mentality.

Why Join Us

• Work directly alongside two of South Florida's top luxury real estate advisors.

• Competitive compensation and performance-based incentives.
• Collaborative, fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment focused on excellence.

jobs.description:
Title: Operations Director

Location: Orlando, Florida

Industry

Electrical contracting, energy solutions, EPC, renewable energy, energy efficiency, distributed energy resources, and operations & maintenance services.

Position Summary

The Operations Director
will lead the launch, growth, and day-to-day execution of a new operation in Orlando, Florida. This role will be responsible for establishing operational infrastructure, building and leading field and project teams, overseeing project execution, driving customer satisfaction, and ensuring all work is delivered safely, on time, within budget, and in alignment with company standards of quality and compliance.

This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role suited for an experienced operations leader with a strong background in electrical construction, EPC, renewable energy, energy efficiency, O&M, or related construction/service environments. The ideal candidate will be capable of scaling a new market while maintaining operational discipline, financial accountability, and a strong field execution culture.

Key Responsibilities

Operations Leadership

Lead the startup and ongoing management of the Orlando operations.
Develop operational processes, workflows, reporting structures, and performance standards for the Florida market.
Oversee daily operations across electrical contracting, energy, service, and maintenance-related projects.
Ensure alignment between field operations, project management, estimating, procurement, safety, and leadership teams.
Build a culture of accountability, urgency, safety, quality, and customer service.

Project & Field Execution

Oversee the successful execution of commercial, industrial, and mission-critical electrical and energy projects.
Monitor project schedules, budgets, manpower planning, subcontractor performance, procurement, and closeout activities.
Partner with Project Managers, Superintendents, Foremen, and field teams to resolve operational issues and maintain project momentum.
Ensure projects are completed on time, within budget, and in accordance with contract requirements, safety standards, and quality expectations.
Support execution of services such as electrical systems, low/medium voltage work, PV solar, energy storage, EV charging, energy efficiency retrofits, commissioning, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, and O&M services, as applicable.

Business Growth & Client Management

Support the growth of the company’s presence in Orlando and the broader Florida market.
Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, owners, general contractors, subcontractors, vendors, and strategic partners.
Identify operational opportunities for service expansion, recurring maintenance, project follow-on work, and long-term client partnerships.
Collaborate with leadership, business development, and estimating teams on market strategy, proposals, project pursuits, and client presentations.
Represent the company professionally in client meetings, site visits, and industry interactions.

Financial & Performance Management

Own operational performance metrics, including profitability, productivity, utilization, safety, quality, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
Review project financials, cost reports, labor productivity, change orders, risks, and margin performance.
Drive corrective actions when projects or teams are trending off schedule, over budget, or below performance expectations.
Support annual budgeting, forecasting, resource planning, and market growth projections.
Ensure effective use of company systems, reporting tools, and operational dashboards.

Team Leadership

Recruit, develop, mentor, and lead operations, project management, and field leadership teams.
Establish clear expectations, accountability structures, and development plans for direct reports.
Promote collaboration between office and field teams to improve execution and communication.
Support workforce planning, field staffing, training, safety compliance, and leadership development.
Foster a high-performance team environment built on trust, discipline, and results.

Safety, Quality & Compliance

Champion a safety-first culture across all operations and job sites.
Ensure compliance with OSHA, company safety standards, client requirements, quality protocols, and applicable codes.
Partner with Safety and Quality teams to conduct audits, address incidents, implement corrective actions, and continuously improve field performance.
Ensure environmental, ethical, and regulatory standards are maintained across all operations.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or related field preferred.
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in electrical construction, EPC, renewable energy, industrial services, construction operations, or related industries.
5+ years in a senior operations leadership role managing project teams, field teams, budgets, and client relationships.
Strong understanding of electrical contracting, construction operations, project controls, field productivity, safety, and financial performance.
Experience launching or scaling operations in a new market is highly preferred.
Experience in commercial, industrial, utility, healthcare, life sciences, institutional, or mission-critical environments is a plus.
Knowledge of PV solar, battery energy storage, EV charging, low/medium voltage systems, energy efficiency, or O&M services is highly desirable.
Strong business acumen with the ability to manage P&L, budgets, forecasts, margins, and operational KPIs.
Demonstrated ability to lead teams, solve complex problems, and drive results in fast-paced environments.
Excellent communication, negotiation, leadership, and client relationship skills.
Bilingual English/Spanish is a plus.
Must be based in or willing to relocate to the Orlando, Florida area.

Ideal Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate is a hands-on, business-minded operations leader who can build a new market from the ground up while maintaining strong execution standards. This person understands both field realities and executive-level business priorities. They are comfortable working in a growing operation, creating structure where needed, holding teams accountable, and building lasting client relationships.
They should bring strong experience in electrical construction, energy services, EPC, or industrial/commercial project execution, with the ability to lead teams, manage financial performance, and represent the organization as a trusted partner in the Florida market.
