new_jobs.title: Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
MHW Search
has exclusively partnered with a well-established retail investment/development firm in Houston in search of a Director of Development.

THE PLATFORM

Our client is a privately held, vertically integrated commercial real estate investment and development firm with in-house capabilities spanning development, construction, brokerage, leasing, and property management.

The company specializes in the development of neighborhood retail centers, grocery-anchored shopping centers, single-tenant build-to-suit projects, and pad-site developments within high-growth markets across Texas and Florida. Through an integrated operating platform, the firm delivers projects from initial site acquisition through development, leasing, disposition, and long-term asset management.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Our client is seeking a Director of Development
to lead build-to-suit and single-tenant development projects from initial site identification through stabilization and disposition. This is a principal-level development role with full lifecycle ownership.

The successful candidate will originate tenant relationships and requirements, source and control development sites, underwrite and structure transactions, negotiate land contracts, oversee due diligence, manage entitlements and permitting, coordinate construction and financing activities, deliver completed projects to tenants, and ultimately guide each asset through stabilization and disposition. Accountability spans the entire development lifecycle, with responsibility for the overall success of each project rather than a single phase.

This position supports two primary business channels. The first involves managing programmatic relationships with regional and national tenants executing multi-unit development programs. In these assignments, the Director serves as the primary point of contact and is responsible for delivering consistent underwriting discipline, schedule execution, communication, and development quality across multiple markets. The second consists of one-off build-to-suit and reverse build-to-suit developments, as well as the single-tenant and pad-site components of larger mixed-use and multi-tenant projects.

The firm operates as a merchant developer, underwriting projects toward defined investment returns and disposition objectives. Success is measured not only by delivering high-quality developments, but by achieving or exceeding the project's targeted financial performance.
This role has also been intentionally designed around technology and operational efficiency. Managing sourcing, entitlements, capital coordination, construction oversight, and dispositions across multiple concurrent developments requires an individual who has fundamentally modernized their development process. Extensive, demonstrable proficiency utilizing artificial intelligence to improve workflow, analysis, documentation, and project execution is considered a core requirement of this position.

REPORTING & STRUCTURE

Reports directly to executive leadership within the Development division.
Serves as the primary point of contact for assigned build-to-suit and reverse build-to-suit clients from initial site presentation through project turnover.
Leads multidisciplinary project teams, including civil engineers, architects, contractors, legal counsel, consultants, and brokerage professionals to ensure successful project execution.
Partners closely with internal construction leadership throughout the development process to coordinate project delivery, scheduling, budgeting, and execution.
Maintains ownership of project schedules, development budgets, and all client-facing communication throughout each assignment.
Collaborates with acquisitions, brokerage, leasing, construction, and executive leadership throughout the development lifecycle, with responsibilities defined based on the specific project.

new_jobs.title: Development Director, School Engagement
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.

We are currently hiring a Development Director, School Engagement,
working with schools in Loudoun, Fairfax, VA; Montgomery, Prince George's, MD, & DC
. This is a full-time, field-based position that requires extensive travel across a few counties in VA, DC, and MD. Flexibility in working hours, including early mornings and evenings, is essential to accommodate the needs of schools and events.

The position is home-office-based, with daily travel within your territory.

In this fast-paced fundraising/sales position, you will engage K-12 students with the Kids Heart Challenge and American Heart Challenge, working with hundreds of schools to promote physical activity and learning. The role also involves extensive data management, continuously updating account information in our customer relationship management (CRM) databases and Microsoft Office products.

Combine your love for fundraising and sales with your passion for kids' health!
The American Heart Association's Kids Heart Challenge
is all about equipping kids with tools to keep their hearts and brains healthy and raising funds to support the health of all hearts. Meet one of our heart heroes here and learn more!

The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. To help you be successful, you will have access to Heart U, our award-winning corporate university, as well as additional training and support locally.

\#TheAHALife is more than a company culture; it is our way of life. It embodies our commitment to work-life harmonization and is guided by our core values where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally. Discover why you will Be Seen. Be Heard. Be Valued at the American Heart Association by following us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs.

Responsibilities

This position is directly responsible for meeting an overall fundraising goal of $350K (this includes participant income and corporate sponsorship) through exceptional volunteer recruitment and engagement, customer service, and account management - all while motivating kids to take their health to heart
.

Recruit and engage students through schools and districts in life-saving initiatives, including the Kids Heart Challenge and the American Heart Challenge programs.
Implement strategies and initiatives to fully engage students through classroom challenges, activities, and student assemblies (in-person and digital experiences).
Develop and cultivate relationships on an ongoing basis with teachers, principals, and district superintendents.
Establish and maintain outstanding customer service with volunteers and other collaborators. This includes detailed planning and kick-off meetings to set schools up for success.
Manage and continuously update account information within our customer relationship management (CRM) databases and Microsoft products.
High volume account management that regularly involves working with 5-10 schools each day - in-person where possible or online/by phone.

Qualifications

3 years of relevant experience in fundraising, sales, or other related experience.
Ability to do daily local travel; requires access to reliable transportation at all times on an immediate basis.
University/College degree or equivalent experience.
Ability to work productively and efficiently from a home office and in the field, consistent with the Association's flexible work arrangements policy.
Demonstrated ability to work independently and communicate proactively.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, "we can do this" environment.
This position demands extensive data management, requiring the continuous updating of account information within our CRM databases; Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to efficiently manage and report on data using CRMs are essential.
Ability to lift and/or move large objects (such as boxes) with the expectation that heavier items would be broken down into smaller components or requesting additional assistance may be required before lifting and/or moving.
Candidates must be willing to work flexible hours, including early mornings and evenings, to effectively engage with schools and manage events.

Here are some of the preferred skills we are looking for:

Experience managing and cultivating volunteer relationships.
Knowledge of corporate and community networks.

Compensation & Benefits

The expected pay range is $61,500 to $80,000. Pay is commensurate with experience; geographic differentials to the pay range may apply. The American Heart Association reserves the right to pay more or less than the posted range. This position is incentive-eligible based on achieving certain targets.

The American Heart Association invests in its people. Here are the main components of our total rewards package. Visit Rewards & Benefits to see more details.

Compensation – Our goal is to ensure you have a competitive base salary. That’s why we regularly review the market value of jobs and make adjustments, as needed.
Performance and Recognition – You are rewarded for achieving success through annual salary planning and incentive programs; this position is incentive eligible based on achieving certain targets.
Benefits – We offer a wide array of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, along with a robust retirement program that includes an employer match and automatic contribution. As a mark of our commitment to employee well-being, we also offer an employee assistance program, employee wellness program, telemedicine, and medical consultation.
Professional Development – You can join one of our many Employee Resource Groups (ERG) or be a mentor/mentee in our professional mentoring program. Heart U is the Association’s national online university, with more than 100,000 resources designed to meet your needs and busy schedule.
Work-Life Harmonization – The Association offers Paid Time Off (PTO) at a minimum of 16 days per year for new employees. The number of days will increase based on seniority level. You will also have a total of 12 paid holidays off each year, which includes several days off at the end of the year.
Tuition Assistance - We support the career development of all employees. This program provides financial assistance to employees who wish to further their education and career in relation to their current duties and responsibilities, or for potential future positions in the organization.

The American Heart Association’s 2028 Goal: Building on over 100 years of trusted leadership in cardiovascular and brain health, by 2028 the Association will drive breakthroughs and implement proven solutions in science, policy, and care for healthier people and communities. The greatest discoveries in health must reach everyone where they are.

At American Heart Association | American Stroke Association, our mission is to be a relentless force for a world of longer, healthier lives, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, age, language, sexual orientation, national origin and physical or cognitive abilities.

We do Consulting Differently

BRG Healthcare supports life sciences companies, payors, providers and their legal teams facing high-stakes investigations and disputes, complex regulations, evolving payment models, and fragmented data systems. This position is based in Chicago, New York, Washington, DC, or Tampa.

This position requires a self-motivated individual with strong communication, leadership, organizational, strategic, and financial analysis skills who can:

Work with HAP experts and senior staff to drive practice strategy, improved financial performance, and growth in revenue and profitability.
Collaborate with BRG’s Financial Planning & Analytics (FP&A) team and HAP leadership to maintain and utilize rolling tracking and forecasting tools to drive financial performance at the practice/expert level, including efforts to achieve revenue, margins, utilization, leverage, and other goals based on key indicators. Act as a liaison between HAP leadership, the ISP community’s Director of Operations, and critical corporate VPs responsible for expert performance review, cross-community staffing and utilization, compensation, and staff performance review and management.
Lead strategic practice initiatives with guidance from HAP leadership, including staffing and utilization management, headcount forecasting, staff performance management, staff learning and development, and practice data management.
Work with HAP leadership to maintain and track various business development budgets and requests for funding.
Work with BRG Business Development professionals across the firm to develop, track, and coordinate BD opportunities, including job pitches, new case opportunities, and marketing events. Develop, support, and coordinate any cross-practice market facing initiatives.
Continue to improve internal communication efforts by working with HAP leadership to describe the practice’s progress and vision to success and growth to all practice members.
Assist in other aspects of practice support as identified by HAP leadership, including preparing meeting agendas, presentations, and updates for the firm’s leadership team and board.
Participate in planning HAP-related activities at the firm’s Managing Director summit and other HAP meetings.
Manage other operational individuals, such as HAP operations managers and ISP operations coordinators.

Expert and Staff Management Liaison

For junior and senior HAP staff, coordinate with HAP leadership and HR for onboarding, utilization management, annual performance management, compensation and bill rate increase processes, and coordinate with the ISP community’s Director of Operations to ensure appropriate level of consistency across the ISP community.
Coordinate with HAP leadership and the ISP community’s Director of Operations regarding staffing needs, utilization, and opportunities to cross-staff resources.
Coordinate with the ISP community’s campus and experienced staff recruiters to support talent pipeline, identify staffing needs, and determine the proper levels of recruiting team resources.
Coordinate with VP of Expert Relations related to expert onboarding and performance management.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate is a consultant or former consultant looking to move into a practice operations leadership role, who has a strategy, management, or finance background in a professional services firm.  Strong problem-solving skills, an entrepreneurial frame of mind, and an ability to drive internal projects independently are all desired.

Specific Skills And Experience Should Include

Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree, MBA, CFA, or CPA a plus
Minimum of 10 years of prior work experience, preferably in a fast-paced consulting environment
Ability to analyze financial information and build financial models for practice management initiatives (e.g., practice profitability, resource planning, compensation modeling, etc.)
Entrepreneurial mindset, with ability to problem solve and think independently and outside-the-box. Excellent written and oral communication skills with a confident and clear communication style
Aptitude to develop insights and recommendations to business problems
Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize changing work demands, and learn quickly
Mature presence, empathy, and intellectual curiosity

Strong understanding of managing relationships and developing solution-based proposals in a professional services environment
Expert working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Ability to travel, primarily to offices with significant presence of HAP staff including Boston, Chicago, New York, Tampa, and Washington, DC

Title: Operations Director

Location: Orlando, Florida

Industry

Electrical contracting, energy solutions, EPC, renewable energy, energy efficiency, distributed energy resources, and operations & maintenance services.

Position Summary

The Operations Director
will lead the launch, growth, and day-to-day execution of a new operation in Orlando, Florida. This role will be responsible for establishing operational infrastructure, building and leading field and project teams, overseeing project execution, driving customer satisfaction, and ensuring all work is delivered safely, on time, within budget, and in alignment with company standards of quality and compliance.

This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role suited for an experienced operations leader with a strong background in electrical construction, EPC, renewable energy, energy efficiency, O&M, or related construction/service environments. The ideal candidate will be capable of scaling a new market while maintaining operational discipline, financial accountability, and a strong field execution culture.

Key Responsibilities

Operations Leadership

Lead the startup and ongoing management of the Orlando operations.
Develop operational processes, workflows, reporting structures, and performance standards for the Florida market.
Oversee daily operations across electrical contracting, energy, service, and maintenance-related projects.
Ensure alignment between field operations, project management, estimating, procurement, safety, and leadership teams.
Build a culture of accountability, urgency, safety, quality, and customer service.

Project & Field Execution

Oversee the successful execution of commercial, industrial, and mission-critical electrical and energy projects.
Monitor project schedules, budgets, manpower planning, subcontractor performance, procurement, and closeout activities.
Partner with Project Managers, Superintendents, Foremen, and field teams to resolve operational issues and maintain project momentum.
Ensure projects are completed on time, within budget, and in accordance with contract requirements, safety standards, and quality expectations.
Support execution of services such as electrical systems, low/medium voltage work, PV solar, energy storage, EV charging, energy efficiency retrofits, commissioning, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, and O&M services, as applicable.

Business Growth & Client Management

Support the growth of the company’s presence in Orlando and the broader Florida market.
Build and maintain strong relationships with clients, owners, general contractors, subcontractors, vendors, and strategic partners.
Identify operational opportunities for service expansion, recurring maintenance, project follow-on work, and long-term client partnerships.
Collaborate with leadership, business development, and estimating teams on market strategy, proposals, project pursuits, and client presentations.
Represent the company professionally in client meetings, site visits, and industry interactions.

Financial & Performance Management

Own operational performance metrics, including profitability, productivity, utilization, safety, quality, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
Review project financials, cost reports, labor productivity, change orders, risks, and margin performance.
Drive corrective actions when projects or teams are trending off schedule, over budget, or below performance expectations.
Support annual budgeting, forecasting, resource planning, and market growth projections.
Ensure effective use of company systems, reporting tools, and operational dashboards.

Team Leadership

Recruit, develop, mentor, and lead operations, project management, and field leadership teams.
Establish clear expectations, accountability structures, and development plans for direct reports.
Promote collaboration between office and field teams to improve execution and communication.
Support workforce planning, field staffing, training, safety compliance, and leadership development.
Foster a high-performance team environment built on trust, discipline, and results.

Safety, Quality & Compliance

Champion a safety-first culture across all operations and job sites.
Ensure compliance with OSHA, company safety standards, client requirements, quality protocols, and applicable codes.
Partner with Safety and Quality teams to conduct audits, address incidents, implement corrective actions, and continuously improve field performance.
Ensure environmental, ethical, and regulatory standards are maintained across all operations.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or related field preferred.
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in electrical construction, EPC, renewable energy, industrial services, construction operations, or related industries.
5+ years in a senior operations leadership role managing project teams, field teams, budgets, and client relationships.
Strong understanding of electrical contracting, construction operations, project controls, field productivity, safety, and financial performance.
Experience launching or scaling operations in a new market is highly preferred.
Experience in commercial, industrial, utility, healthcare, life sciences, institutional, or mission-critical environments is a plus.
Knowledge of PV solar, battery energy storage, EV charging, low/medium voltage systems, energy efficiency, or O&M services is highly desirable.
Strong business acumen with the ability to manage P&L, budgets, forecasts, margins, and operational KPIs.
Demonstrated ability to lead teams, solve complex problems, and drive results in fast-paced environments.
Excellent communication, negotiation, leadership, and client relationship skills.
Bilingual English/Spanish is a plus.
Must be based in or willing to relocate to the Orlando, Florida area.

Ideal Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate is a hands-on, business-minded operations leader who can build a new market from the ground up while maintaining strong execution standards. This person understands both field realities and executive-level business priorities. They are comfortable working in a growing operation, creating structure where needed, holding teams accountable, and building lasting client relationships.
They should bring strong experience in electrical construction, energy services, EPC, or industrial/commercial project execution, with the ability to lead teams, manage financial performance, and represent the organization as a trusted partner in the Florida market.

new_jobs.title: Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
About The Organization

Figure Skating in Harlem is a nonprofit organization entering its 30th anniversary of dedication to empowering girls and young women through education, leadership development, and access to opportunity through the sport of figure skating. As the organization enters a transformative period of growth—including a major capital initiative to build its own rink—we are seeking a strategic, highly organized, and proactive Director of Development to help lead and execute our fundraising efforts.

Position Summary

The Director of Development supports the Chief Growth Officer in executing the organization’s annual fundraising strategy across individual giving, institutional giving, corporate partnerships, donor stewardship, and special events. This role will serve as the operational lead for development activities and work closely with the Chief Growth Officer to support revenue growth, strengthen donor engagement, and build sustainable fundraising systems. The Director of Development will oversee all planning, coordination, and execution of the organization’s annual gala and other fundraising events, managing all pre-event logistics internally while partnering with external consultants and vendors for design support and day-of event execution. This position will also play a growing role in corporate sponsorship strategy and relationship management. Corporate partnerships will initially be a shared responsibility with senior leadership and transition more fully to this role over time. The Director of Development will work collaboratively with the organization’s Director of Communications & External Affairs to ensure alignment across fundraising, government relations, corporate engagement, communications, and institutional strategy. The role will also receive operational and administrative support from a shared Development & Operations Coordinator. The ideal candidate is strategic, highly organized, self-directed, and execution-oriented.

Key Responsibilities

Development Strategy & Revenue Execution

Partner with the Chief Growth Officer to execute the organization’s annual fundraising plan and revenue strategy, especially major donor cultivation, stewardship, and solicitation efforts
Manage timelines, deliverables, and execution across fundraising initiatives
In coordination with Chief Growth Officer, maintain and strengthen donor pipelines and moves management systems; prepare donor materials, briefing documents, proposals, and stewardship reports
Track fundraising performance and provide regular reporting and analysis
Proactively identify opportunities, challenges, and operational needs across the development function

Institutional Giving & Grants

Manage grant calendar, deadlines, reporting, and submissions for non-government funders
Draft and coordinate foundation and institutional grant proposals and reports
Maintain relationships and records for private and institutional funders
Ensure compliance with grant requirements and reporting timelines

Gala & Special Event

Serve as project lead for the organization’s annual gala and fundraising events
Manage all pre-event planning, coordination, timelines, logistics, and internal execution
Oversee sponsorship outreach and fulfillment, invitation management, auction coordination, seating, vendor coordination, and event communications
Partner with external consultants and vendors on graphic design, production support, and day-of event execution
Manage post-event stewardship and donor follow-up plans
Collaborate with board members, host committees, and leadership to drive event fundraising success

Young Professionals Board Management

Serve as primary staff lead for the organization’s Young Professionals Board
Manage board communications, meetings, engagement strategies, and event coordination
Support fundraising initiatives, membership cultivation, and volunteer leadership development

Corporate Partnerships

Support development and stewardship of corporate sponsorship relationships
Work collaboratively with senior leadership and the Director of Communications & External Affairs on sponsorship strategy and outreach
Over time, assume increasing ownership of corporate partnership management and revenue generation

Development Operations & Stewardship

Partner with the Development & Operations Coordinator to oversee donor acknowledgment and stewardship systems
Ensure database accuracy, gift processing integrity, and strong donor record management
Oversee gift reconciliation processes between development and finance
Improve systems and workflows to increase efficiency and donor experience

Qualifications

5-8 years of progressively responsible, nonprofit development experience
Proven experience independently managing fundraising events and complex projects
Strong writing and communication skills, including experience in grant writing
Experience managing multiple fundraising streams and deadlines simultaneously
Ability to work independently and proactively in a fast-paced environment
Demonstrated self-direction, initiative, and strong project ownership
Highly organized with strong project management skills and attention to detail
Collaborative, solutions-oriented, and adaptable

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in arts, education, youth development, or mission-driven organizations
Experience supporting capital campaigns or major organizational growth initiatives
Experience with Raiser’s Edge preferred
Knowledge of the figure skating landscape, including familiarity with the skating community, competitive ecosystem, relationships within the sport and/or passion for sports-based youth development

Required To Apply

A cover letter detailing your interest in Figure Skating in Harlem’s mission, experience, and qualifications
Resume
A work sample or project for which you were the primary producer (annual report, grant, proposal, etc, redacted if needed)
